It was played often in the FCA01 tour along with the original Beat of Death, often alongside Ballad For The Lost Dancer. The crowds were almost always completely silent out of respect.
trackinfo.credits: from chxpped and lxxped, released November 21, 2017

Friendly Clip Art Collective.title: friendly_clip_art.00
Friendly Clip Art Collective.about:
3000-3003
on janurary 1st, 3000, the one-thousand year anniversary of the climax of the First Collapse, the artist known as Friendly Clip Art - then only known as the drummer for a few small-time 20th-century-revival rock bands - got on stage and debuted their new project. the music environment in what is now nervously being called "the Third Collapse" is heavily reliant on borrowing from pre-apocalypse sounds, as many want to reach back to seemingly better times and ignore the decay around them - indeed, many deny a third collapse at all. from the very start, the goal of FCA was to undermine this perception; with a minimal style using cheap electronics, they hoped to provide a sound more accurate to the fading world around them. due to a lack of refinement this of course wasn't received well at first, but the project would go on.
early FCA was admittedly somewhat aimless and quiet - while they were soundtracking a movie known as "_ZZANX.wav", it was never finished owing to the director's disappearance and the whole affair doesn't hold much relevance for what would eventually become the central goal of the FCA Collective. early live shows and projects had the same 'trashy' digital sound that would carry the Collective through their first half-decade, but it wasn't until FCA met Unknown Classical at a show that they would start to come into their own. the two had similar ideas on what led to their current situation and what the future would be like, and eventually decided to formally form the Collective with the goal of documenting in music the history of the world from the first flashes of the First Collapse to where they believe the Third Collapse will end up, a project still in motion to this day.
while the FCA Collective formally started in 3001 and work on friendly_clip_art.01 began shortly after, the album would not release until 3003 due to a variety of setbacks, such as FCA's continuing career as "DJ Terrible", general struggles on settling on one specific vision, and personal tragedies. while these delays could frustrate those keeping up with them, a constant stream of live shows (eventually centralized in a homemade venue that could stream recorded footage to other screens, an increasingly rare feature) helped sustain a small but growing dedicated fanbase. you know the rest from here, of course - more artists joining the collective, controversies over fca01's release, an eventual shift away from improvisation elevating the Collective into one of the most essential acts of the 3000s, and so on. this album, then, is an odds'n'ends for the more obscure bits of their earliest incarnations, featuring snippets from the first ever FCA live show, selected tracks from the _ZZANX.wav soundtrack, and several demos and outtakes from fca01. please enjoy in the time you have left before the Third Collapse hits its climax!

Friendly Clip Art Collective.title: friendly_clip_art.01: Play
Friendly Clip Art Collective.about:
1949-1980
a recollected hallucination of prenuclear america in the height of artistic innovation and societal collapse, told through the story of "The Dancer", real-world creator of several artistically innovative and challenging musical plays. these plays eschewed conventional musical form and narrative format, typically being drum-led and abstractly-told (often lacking dialogue or being presented out of order), incorporating unusual and new instruments and serving as the inspiration for countless artists - including, over a thousand years later, Friendly Clip Art.
created in the rough musical style of archived plays, fca01 narrates the life of The Dancer. the first half looks at his pre-fame background as an african native, kidnapped by the french as a teenager to serve as a soldier in one of many chaotic, brutal wars following the cold war's implosion. these experiences gave him a burning hatred not just for the country which stole his former life but for government in general for bringing humanity to this point - this ideology would be crucial in his later art.
the second half fast-forwards to show The Dancer in his later years as a mature, refined artist and political figurehead, his burning passion molded into a sharp and cutting worldview. while he never achieved true mainstream success his work and writings were influential and convincing enough that he became well-known as a political figure, and was one of many at the base of a growing leftist movement in the years leading up to the first collapse. on a sweltering night in june, in the wake of a looming worldwide insurrection, rogue government officials decided they couldn't risk his views gaining any further ground. his car was sabotaged, and he was caught in a fatal accident on his way to an early-morning performance.
though an outpouring of support was given following this tragic event, it was not until later that the government's role in The Dancer's passing became known, and by then (despite the usa's best efforts) protests and riots had gotten to a point so intense that his passing was only a drop in the bucket. through hundreds of years of turmoil and long periods of obscurity and rediscovery his work was preserved, in recordings and transcripts and sheet music and simple recollection, enduring enough for the FCA Collective to follow in his footsteps and paint a portrait not just of The Dancer but of the period of turmoil and gradual decaying collapse he found himself a victim of.
[warning: wartime fantasies and nightlife contain sudden, loud noises]

Friendly Clip Art Collective.about:
2307-2413
this album tells the story of the Weapon, the Angel, and the Revival, which took place over a little more than a century. at the end of the world, approaching the bottom of its slow death spiral, a Weapon created to speed this death, who destroyed everything around it, was taught to feel by the Angel and instigated the Revival, and the world was brought back to life. see story PDF in download for more details.
this project took two years of solid work to record, illustrate, and write, not counting all the time spent before as it took shape. we hope you enjoy the fruits of our labor.

Friendly Clip Art Collective.title: Never the Same...
Friendly Clip Art Collective.about:
an album of experimental, semi-improvisatory jams recorded two years before nanoempathy but released in another world, now brought here for your listening pleasure.
1999-2002
at the end of the millennium, two simultaneous uprisings occurring in the USA and USSR threatened to overthrow their governments and upturn the world order constructed over the course of the cold war. the governments of both states had begun to collapse in the decades prior and revolutionary movements, seeing their increasingly obvious failures and evil, coalesced into full anarchist insurrections. on new years eve, 1999, the usa made a decision that would send the world into a seemingly endless spiral of death and destruction, and - with government officials and other high-ranking peoples having fled to underground bunkers - launched a nuclear attack on its own soil against the revolutionaries. the ussr's failing automatic systems detected these attacks but were unable to launch their weapons, simply detonating them - again - on their own soil. the worst had come to pass, and while the worldwide effects would not immediately be felt, soon large parts of the surface would become barren and the First Collapse would nearly kill global civilization.
this album is about those events, and the uncanniness of living through them and their immediate aftermath, where people had not yet been forced to flee underground by radioactivity and climate collapse and still lived in the newly-emptied husks of what had been.
